t:
Section 114(b) (2) of the District of Columbia Sales Tax Act (D.C. Code, sec. 47–2601, par. 14(b)(2)) is amended to read as follows:


“(2) 

(A) 
Sales of transportation and communication services other than sales of local telephone service.


“(B) 
Sales of local telephone service rendered by means of a coin-operated telephone available to the public; except that where such coin-operated telephone service is furnished for a guaranteed amount, the amounts paid under such guarantee plus any fixed monthly or other periodic charge shall be subject to the tax impend on local telephone service by this title.”

fable.w: This section only amends the District of Columbia Sales Tax Act to define which transportation, communication and telephone service sales are taxed or exempt. The tempting reading is that "available to the public" signals public involvement, but the phrase merely describes coin-operated telephones. No outside party is consulted, heard, placed on an advisory body, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.
fable.s: Sales of local telephone service rendered by means of a coin-operated telephone available to the public

qwen_block.w: This section defines the scope of taxable sales for local telephone services. It does not require the government to consult with, coordinate with, or receive input from any outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The mention of the 'public' refers only to the availability of the service, not to public participation in the regulatory process.
qwen_block.s: Sales of local telephone service rendered by means of a coin-operated telephone available to the public; except that where such coin-operated telephone service is furnished for a guaranteed amount, the amounts paid under such guarantee plus any fixed monthly or other periodic charge shall be subject to the tax impend on local telephone service by this title.
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions services "available to the public," it involves the public. However, this is merely a definition of what constitutes a taxable transaction (a coin-operated phone). It does not require the government to consult with the public, hold a hearing, or coordinate with outside entities before making a decision. It is a substantive tax provision, not a procedural participation mechanism.

opus.w: This amendment only changes which transportation and communication services, including coin-operated telephone service, count as taxable sales under the D.C. Sales Tax Act. The phrase "available to the public" describes the telephones, not any public role in a decision. The section creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue, so it has no participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends a tax statute to define which sales are taxable. It does not require the government to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from any outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The mention of services 'available to the public' describes the nature of the taxable activity, not a participatory process. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the tax applies to services "available to the public," it involves the public. However, the definition of participation requires the government to consult or coordinate with outside parties *before* making a decision. This section merely defines the scope of a tax; it does not require any consultation, hearing, or comment period from the public or other outside entities regarding the imposition of the tax. The public is the subject of the regulation, not a participant in the decision-making process.
